name: crypto_id
description: Identify the encryption scheme a volume's or file's first bytes show, and say what they do not. Reads: the BitLocker and BitLocker To Go signatures (no protectors), LUKS1 header fields and its eight-slot table, the LUKS2 binary header (version, label, UUID; the keyslots, digests, segments and tokens are cryptsetup luksDump's), Apple Core Storage and APFS container signatures (whether an APFS volume is encrypted is not read), and ZIP, 7-Zip, PDF and OLE signatures (their protection is archive_probe's, which is itself partly heuristic). An unsupported LUKS version or a cut-short header is named (status partial), not guessed. VeraCrypt and TrueCrypt leave no signature: high entropy over the sample is one lead among several, never an identification, and no match is never 'not encrypted'. Every answer says the next reader and what is not determined, and carries status and status_basis. It prints no raw bytes of the file (include_head_hex, which printed the first 32, is gone: a 32-byte file is a usual key file, and a call that asks for it is refused with that said); the header's text fields are printed only when they are what the format says: the LUKS cipher, mode and hash only from the closed lists of the names cryptsetup and the kernel use, the UUID only in the UUID form, anything else as '<unrecognised header text withheld>' (header_fields_withheld names the fields), and the LUKS2 label and subsystem, which are free text, with every part shaped like an identifier or a secret withheld; the header's numbers (sizes, counts, a slot state) and the entropy of the sample are printed. The path is printed the same way. It stops on SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP with one answer and exit 128 + the signal, a read that has not returned after 105 seconds ends it with one partial answer (exit 0; the stop is the clock's, not the work's: a page fault or a read that sits in the system cannot be ended until the call returns), and a file it cannot read is an error answer, not a traceback. Withholding is by shape, measured on random draws per shape planted in a member name or path (rates, not guarantees). Printed whole in 0 of 1,000 draws: hexadecimal ids of 16, 32 and 64, numbers of 10 digits or more, recovery passwords written with dashes, spaces, dots, underscores, no separator or one to three of any other characters between the groups (an en dash, a comma, a colon, a pipe, a tab), also when the groups are cut at the separators of the path (123456-123456/123456-...), full-width, split by invisible characters, or with one decimal digit glued to the first or last group, AWS access key ids, password= and api_key: assignments, user-info, 4x4 groups of capitals and digits joined by - or ., letters and digits of 8, 9, 12, 16 or 40 characters that hold a capital, a small letter and a digit, and a full-width id. Printed whole in some draws: uniform draws of letters and digits (every character as likely a capital, a small letter or a digit as any other) of 8 characters about 2.5%, of 9 about 2%, of 12 about 1%, of 16 about 0.6%, of 24 at most 0.1% and of 40 none; random lowercase letters and digits of 8 about 7%, of 12 about 2.4%, of 16 about 0.4%; 24 random letters 1.5% to 2.6%; a 16-character base32 id 2.2% to 3.4% (by alphabet); four groups of four lowercase hexadecimal digits joined by underscores 4% to 9% (by how the draws are made); an id of 12 or 16 characters whose letters are half Cyrillic or Greek look-alikes about 1%. NOT recognised, by design, and printed whole: an identifier of 7 characters or fewer, a number of 9 digits or fewer, a lowercase-only run of up to 22 letters (it reads as a word), an all-capital letters-only run of any length, three groups of four or five capitals and digits joined by - or . (a rule for them would also withhold upper-case constants such as OpenSSL manual page names), a recovery password cut by anything other than a separator or with a letter in it or glued to it (the groups then show), a ten-digit number written 3-3-4, an e-mail-like lowercase string, and a secret of any other shape; a file whose secrets matter is read in a job run with secret_output: true. What the rule is given is bounded: a string of more than 4096 characters (as written or after folding), a path of more than 8192, or a string with a / and a run of more than 256 name characters is withheld whole as '<text too long to judge withheld>' and not judged (the slowest string inside the bound that a search found took 0.13 CPU s). The output check, which reads every printed string once more, is narrower than the rule: with the rule removed it replaces recovery passwords (full-width ones too), AWS ids, password= values, PEM headers, user-info, hexadecimal of 16 digits or more and runs of 24 or more characters that flip between letters and digits, and it lets through numbers of 10 to 20 digits, ids of up to 23 characters, some base64 (about one in five of 32 bytes), every recovery password whose groups are joined by anything but a hyphen, underscore, dot, space or nothing, and every recovery password cut over the components of a path (the first layer alone holds those). The rule also changes names that are not secrets: of the file names of a documents tree 6.9% have a part withheld (10-digit timestamps, UUIDs) and 0.6% of its directories, of an application tree 16% and 3.1% (a word with a digit inside, such as libmp3lame, is withheld in part).

path.description: A volume image, a partition, or a file

offset.description: Byte offset of the volume within the image (bytes, not sectors)

entropy_sample.description: Bytes to sample for the no-signature case (default 65536, from 1024 to 16777216)
